descriptionChirho: The verb 'asah in the Qal stem means 'to do' or 'to make', encompassing both the sense of performing an action and constructing/creating something. All four clusters are Qal forms with only conjugational variation (perfect 2fs, perfect 3ms, conjunctive perfect 1cs, imperfect 2ms). Multilingual glosses confirm a unified semantic range: Spanish 'hiciste/hizo/hare/hagas' (all forms of 'hacer'), Hindi 'banaye tune/banaya/karunga/kar', Arabic 'sana'ti/sana'a/asna'u/taf'al', Korean 'haenghayeotda/mandeulyeotda/haenghagetta/haenghara', and Swahili 'ulifanya/alitengeneza/nitakufanyia/fanya'. These are inflectional variants of a single Qal sense, not distinct meanings.
